top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is the only proposal on the slate and the only one I can support on literary grounds. His voice is distinctive. As publicly described, the Orbitor sequence (Blinding is its first volume) and Solenoid build memory, the body and dream into one sustained imaginative system with large formal architecture and real intellectual depth. The major structures exist, so the oeuvre can be assessed as a whole now. Attribution is clean: one writer, one language, with a prose-centred citation that names the poetry as foundation and does not rest the award on it. The round-2 exchange found no literary reason to prefer no award. The remaining doubts concern evidence, not quality: how much of the Romanian sentence-level density survives translation, whether the later volumes advance the project or only enlarge it, and how much the poetry can bear. These rest on public knowledge and translation-mediated access, not independent reading or verification. Unanimity in the opening is not evidence of merit. P000 is ranked second because those doubts do not amount to a case against the writer.
